## Confirmed findings
- [Should-fix] D5 'Busy and idle come from engine events, keyed by turn id'; D5 Restart; D8 'Rewriting them on upgrade is safe, because Claude Code reloads plugin directories' — A mod reload mid-turn (routine on every setup upgrade) wipes the open-turn set, so the mod treats a running session as idle and calls $.prompt.submit while a main turn is open, recreating the queued-submit/Esc-takeover race.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/interface.md 'Keep state': a module-level variable lasts 'until the module reloads'; `$.state` 'survives a reload of the module, which a variable doesn't'. Spike README row 8: hot reload gives 'Module state reset'. The spec persists only the dedup set in `$.store` (D5 line 144) and defines no initial busy state after a reload. D8 makes reloads routine on every `setup claude`. All three seats could find no turn-state getter in the spec; D10 checks the invariant only against the mod's own model.
  fix-shape hint: start in an assumed-busy state after load until the first turn.complete or an observed idle, or keep open turn ids in `$.state`; add reload-mid-turn to the D10 interleavings and specify recovery for a stale open id (lost turn.complete).

- [Should-fix] D6 'When a delivery resolves (context returned from the hook chain, submit resolved, append resolved), the mod runs herdr-threads watch ack' — $.prompt.submit and $.session.append can resolve with {drop}/{deny} or a rewritten row, yet D6 acks on mere resolution without inspecting the result, settling receipts under cooperative_mod_delivery for text that never entered context.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts PromptSubmitResult is a union with `{ drop: string }`: 'The prompt did not enter: a hook's refusal, answered without `next`, or a settings hook's block beneath.' `$.prompt.submit` returns `Promise<PromptSubmitResult>`, so a dropped submit resolves normally. Spec D6 (line 155) acks on 'submit resolved' and nowhere branches on drop or deny; AckModDelivered cannot see the drop. The session.append {deny} half was not re-fetched by any seat; the submit half carries the finding.
  fix-shape hint: ack only when the resolved value has no drop/deny and the text matches; treat a drop as not delivered (items stay pending, log it, back off); add a UserPromptSubmit-exit-2 spike row.

- [Should-fix] D7 'On disconnect ... The registry entry is removed. The wake lane is kicked' vs D12 'Reconnect grace. When a watch connection drops, the daemon waits 30 s before the native kick' — D7 removes the registry entry on disconnect while D12 only defers the native kick for 30 s, so new attention during the grace window triggers native wake alongside the reconnecting mod (or, if suppressed, adds 30 s of silence).
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: D7 (lines 185-188) names three registry consumers (NativeWakeDispatcher::attempt / can_reserve_poke, hook digest, scheduler kick) and says the entry 'is removed' on disconnect. D12 (line 269) changes only the timing of 'the native kick' and keeps no tombstone. Neither text says whether a channel in grace counts as live, so a message published 5 s into a reload's grace can go native while the mod re-registers and re-streams it. Refute seat's point that at-least-once is accepted covers only an 'unrecovered handoff', not items arriving during a recovered reload (challenge 4).
  fix-shape hint: one sentence in D12: an entry in reconnect grace counts as live for all three D7 consumers (or state that new attention is deferred during grace and the 30 s silence is accepted).

- [Should-fix] D5 table (busy column) and D6 'context returned from the hook chain' — Acking when the tool.call hook returns context assumes the text reaches the model, but a denied/interrupted tool call, an outer mod or the managed tier can strip it afterwards, settling receipts for undelivered text.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: claude-code.d.ts ToolCallResult: the deny variant has `context?: undefined` ('Refuses the call: the model receives the text as an error result'); the `isError: true` variant is for a call that 'threw, was interrupted, or answered an error'; only the answered-result variant carries `context`. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/events.md: 'When you call `next(e)`, Claude Code runs the permission check and then the tool'; 'The first mod is outermost: it sees the event before the others and the result after them.' Spec D5/D6 never say which result shapes count as delivered. Refute seat's point that the hook sees the deny before settling is correct and is exactly what the spec fails to require.
  fix-shape hint: ack only when the final result is the answered-result variant that carried the context; re-queue on deny or isError; state it in D6 and add a deny/Esc spike row (outer-mod stripping stays unverified).

While idle: $.session.append at once; it starts no turn'); D6 'append resolved'; D6 'The claim is "the full body entered the model's context through the mod"' — Lazy rows appended while idle are acked as displayed when append resolves, but the row only reaches the model on the next turn, so a /clear or exit first leaves a completed lazy row for text the model never saw.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: Spike row 5: idle append 'No turn started. Claude read it on the next user turn.' D6 completes lazy ids 'as displayed (A8), with the same claim' at append resolution; D12 re-streams after /clear only acks refused as stale. Severity set to Nit on the refute seat's TRUST-POLICY A8 evidence (lazy completion is 'idempotent presentation bookkeeping', no receipt, no ACK evidence), which the ground seat concedes: nothing downstream relies on the claim, and the claim's "settled receipt" wording is overstated for lazy rows.
  fix-shape hint: reword the lazy-append claim to 'appended to the transcript', or defer the lazy ack to the next main turn.start.

- [Nit] D12 Generation: 'Those items re-stream to the new session, whose context no longer holds them'; D12 'A generation change discards the set' — Refusing stale-generation acks and re-streaming is wrong for /resume, whose restored transcript already holds the deliveries, so the same item enters that context twice.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: D12 lines 266-267 rotate the generation on '(`/clear`, resume)' and say the new context 'no longer holds them'; line 284 discards the delivered-but-unacked set on any generation change. Spike rows 5 and 7: an appended row 'was still there after /resume' and `/resume <id>` switches the id back. Only items delivered-but-unacked at the moment of resume are affected; the result is a duplicate, never a loss (hence Nit), but challenge 4 names '/resume' under 'without loss or duplication'.
  fix-shape hint: keep the de-dup set keyed by session id across generation changes (discard on /clear only), or list the resume duplicate as an accepted limit.

- [Should-fix] D12 'Failed acks are retried'; D6 'Refuses anything else: unknown ids; truncated ids; ids not addressed to the seat; a stale generation' — watch ack is not specified as idempotent and the mod cannot tell terminal refusals (already settled, unknown) from transient failures, so refused ids are retried until a generation change.
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✗ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: D6 lists four refusals and defines no result for an id already settled (the agent can run `inbox`/ACK on a receipt the mod delivered but has not acked yet); D6 never says 'idempotent' and never says whether a refusal is per id or fails the whole `watch ack` batch. D12 says only 'Failed acks are retried. A generation change discards the set.' The exit-code table covers the `watch` stream process, not `watch ack`. Reproduce seat's REJECT concedes the gap exists and argues only that retries are bounded by the generation lifetime.
  fix-shape hint: define acking an already-settled id as idempotent success (or a distinct terminal result), make refusals per id, and give `watch ack` terminal vs retryable result codes so the mod drops terminal ids from its retry set.

- [Should-fix] D8 install via env.CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS; D8 'older versions simply never load the mod, which is the fallback' — The managed setting `disableSideloadFlags` also covers `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`, so writing it into user settings on a managed machine makes Claude Code exit at startup instead of falling back. [lanes: domain:plugin-integration]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md (`disableSideloadFlags`): 'The same check covers plugin folders named in the `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` environment variable ... ## Rejected (with reason)
- D7 stall definition; D12 'Stall handover'; D5 busy row — Stall rule cannot distinguish a >10-minute tool call from a stuck mod. Rejected 2-1: the stall bound is an explicit D7 'Considered' tradeoff ('one stuck mod would silence a seat forever'), the post-stall state is the pre-mod native ladder with the existing composer guards, nothing is lost. Ground seat's dissent (false positive on a healthy busy session, D12 line 270) is a tuning concern the majority addresses; a mod-side 'busy, holding' keepalive is an optional improvement.
- D4 limits (8 KiB, 64 KiB pages); D5 context attach; D6 'full body entered' — Mod context subject to the 10k hook additionalContext cap. Rejected 3-0: claude-code.d.ts ToolCallResult.context says 'any length: past 100,000 (200,000 together) head + path'; the 10k cap is documented for settings hooks only. Residue: no cap on total context per tool result (needs ~12+ max-size messages queued in one tool call), a possible Nit.
- D7 stall definition ('some ordinary pending receipt'); D12 'Attention items ... never acked' — Stall bound counts only ordinary receipts, so attention/truncated/lazy items can be held indefinitely. Rejected 2-1: the Esc-and-walk-away story is bounded by the 120 s hold and D12 Drafts; attention also attaches to the next tool.call; the residual (wedged mod plus attention-only pending) is not a spec-stated scenario and attention has no ack signal to key a stall on.
- Key decisions 'doubles as the liveness signal'; D7 stall rule — No mod-level heartbeat; wedged worker keeps registration live. Rejected 3-0: the D7/D12 stall rule is the chosen progress-based liveness bound and D7 rejects hard suppression explicitly; challenge 1 covers lost connections, which D2 handles.
- D5 De-duplication; D12 'Delivered-but-unacked ids' — $.store 4 MiB shared store never pruned. Rejected 2-1: the daemon's pending receipt is the cursor and authority; a lost dedup set degrades to the accepted at-least-once duplicate; reaching 4 MiB takes hundreds of thousands of ids. Ground seat's Nit (document pruning and a failed `set` fallback) is a wording suggestion.
- D4 'paging until drained'; Key decisions 'Cursor' — No keyset cursor, permanently pending items refill every page. Rejected 3-0: D4 sources pages from `InboxBatch`-style pages and `lazy_delivery::pending_page`, which carry existing continuation cursors (src/protocol/pagination.rs InboxBatchV2CursorState; pending_page takes `after`/`high_water`). Wording nit: 'drained' should mean cursor exhausted, not pending set empty.
- Key decisions 'watch fetches ... through existing read paths'; D6 cooperative_inbox_display — Fetch might settle receipts on flush. Rejected 3-0: src/protocol/commands.rs:34-36 documents InboxBatch as read-only with a separate accountable ACK command; cooperative_inbox_display is written only on the ack path (src/store/receipts.rs:194).
- D2 Close{replaced}; D12 exit-code table — No Close reason mapped to an exit code; two mod instances evict each other forever. Rejected 3-0: needs two live mod instances in one session (a misconfiguration the spec does not claim to cover); on reload the old child dies with its parent (getppid poll) and session.end stops the child before restart; churn would be bounded by backoff and id de-dup.
- D12 exit codes '3 | permanent: disabled, no HERDR_PANE_ID, unsupported' — Sessions stay inert after daemon upgrade or mod_delivery toggle. Rejected 2-1: the fallback is hooks plus wake by design and nothing is lost; `setup claude` rewrites mod files and reloads; the operator toggle reading at registration is intended. Ground seat's Nit (slow retry for 'unsupported') is an operability suggestion.
- D8 'Rewriting them on upgrade is safe, because Claude Code reloads plugin directories' — Non-atomic rewrite of three files mid-reload. Rejected 2-1: a failed load ends in the native-wake fallback; the write completing re-fires a save reload; the crash-to-unload chain is unverified. Ground seat's Nit (temp-file plus rename, register.js last) is cheap hardening worth a line.
- D2 'a daemon restart drops all of them; the clients reconnect'; D12 Reconnect grace — No boot grace after daemon restart, duplicate native wake. Rejected 3-0: D7/D12 accept at-least-once across a handoff; mods re-ack from $.store rather than re-deliver; mods reconnect within ~1 s.
- D6 'a live watch registration for that generation'; D12 Stall handover — Acks refused during the stall lockout re-deliver natively. Rejected 3-0: a stall close is a handoff and D7/D12 accept at-least-once across handoffs; delivered-but-unacked ids persist and re-ack after the window.
- D2 'pushes WatchFrame values'; D7 scheduler kick — No non-blocking send, bounded queue or Attention coalescing. Rejected 2-1: frames are tiny version markers; the stall rule bounds a wedged reader; write mechanics are implementation detail. Ground seat's Nit (coalesce to latest version, write deadline) is a one-line clarification.
- D4 truncation rule; D12 'Items the stream marked truncated never count toward a stall' — Ignored truncated item has no reminder path. Rejected 2-1: the first 8 KiB plus the `body <id>` hint is delivered; withholding the ack is deliberate honesty; reconnect re-streams pending items; per-message reminder policy is out of scope (ht-tqx).
- D12 'Attention items ... re-sent once per attention version and after each watch (re)start'; D5 idle rule — Every restart starts a fresh turn for the same marker. Rejected 3-0: D4 gives attention items a stable id and D5's delivered-id set in $.store de-duplicates them; refusals never register so never re-send; spec could say attention ids are covered.
- D3 retry policy; D11 claude -p exclusion; D8 env — Nested claude inherits HERDR_PANE_ID and retries session_mismatch forever. Rejected 2-1: the refusal grants nothing, retries are bounded by the nested process lifetime, cost is one spawn per 30 s. Ground seat's Nit (treat repeated session_mismatch as permanent) is cheap hardening; D11's stated reason is imprecise.
- D5 'Events carrying agentId are ignored'; D12 'Subagent tool calls never carry context' — agentId documented only for tool.check. Rejected 3-0: claude-code.d.ts AgentLoop.agentId is on tool.call ('the same string its loop's tool.call events carry as agentId') and turn.complete; the spike mod already filters on e.agentId. Residue: spike README line 92 lists subagent calls as not exercised.
- D5 'a set of open main-conversation turn ids' — Skipped turn.complete leaves a stale id forever. Rejected 3-0: the hook does microseconds of work under a 10 s own-execution limit; a stuck set is bounded by the D7/D12 stall handover, an accepted tradeoff; context delivery is unaffected.
- D2 'pushes WatchFrame values'; Main challenges 1 — No push mechanism specified. Rejected 3-0: D2 adds the WatchRequest connection kind and the (seat, generation) → connection registration; D7 names ModChannels and the scheduler kick that 'also notifies channels'; the lost-wakeup window is covered by notify-then-fetch over the pending-state cursor.
- D5 '$.prompt.submit of one batched, framed text'; D4 'paging until drained' — No cap on items/bytes per delivery. Rejected 2-1: no stated requirement is contradicted; the submit size limit claim is unverified; backlog is the same pending messages the agent would read via paged inbox. Ground seat's Nit (per-delivery cap, e.g. one page) is optional hardening.
- D6 ack through $.process.run; D7 Handoff — $.store write not ordered before delivery; crash re-delivers. Rejected 3-0: D7/D12 state 'at-least-once across a handoff, and never lost (an accepted limit)'; the D10 at-most-once invariant is a stubbed-test property, not a cross-crash guarantee.
- D6 settle on delivery; D12 Generation — Compaction drops a settled message. Rejected 3-0: D6 states the user-approved claim ('delivery is the receipt', 'not a proof that the model read it'); compaction is outside challenge 4's list; the native path has the same exposure; bodies remain reachable via `body <id>`.
- D5 'One submit in flight' — No timeout for a hung $.prompt.submit. Rejected 3-0: the permission-dialog case is unreachable because D5 never submits while a turn is open; a hung submit is bounded by the stall rule; session.end restarts the child. Nit: say the in-flight flag resets on session.end.

Rejected 3-0: D10 states the skip and gating with recorded reasons; the spec makes no CI-placement requirement; engine drift degrades to stall handover and native wake (D9 accepted limits trust engine idleness).

Rejected 3-0: fallback to native wake is the stated contract; D3 refusals are typed; per-seat diagnostics is an unstated requirement. Nit-level improvement at most.
- D1 $.process.spawn; D5 $.session.append; D8 version gate — Early-access API, append/spawn absent from d.ts. Rejected 3-0: the GitHub d.ts header is 'Written by Claude Code 2.1.277', older than the 2.1.287 gate and the 2.1.294 spike; the mods reference (as of v2.1.290) lists `append` under $.session and `run, spawn` under $.process; D12's startup check keeps the mod inert without the APIs. Nit: gate on the spike version or a behavioural smoke test.
- D3 'recorded as a channel claim with ... cooperative_mod_channel'; D2 'held in memory only'; D9 A3/A5 — No stored artifact for the provenance. Rejected 2-1: 'recorded' in D3 labels the same process-local registration D2 describes; D9 A3 scopes it to 'channel registrations only' and A5 rows are authority rules. Ground seat's Nit: say explicitly it is an in-memory label.

Rejected 2-1: the whole block is framed as untrusted data, sender/thread/relays_user are daemon fields, and the trust model forbids adversarial hardening. Ground seat's Nit cites src/cli/hook.rs:368 and src/harness/claude.rs:458-466 to show the hook convention JSON-escapes peer data while the spec's block does not; worth a one-line note (JSON-encode the body) but not material under the cooperative model.

Rejected 3-0: spike README line ~51 confirms the wrapper, but waking the agent to address the message is the goal; the mod's header survives inside the frame; the cooperative model makes authority differences immaterial.
- D5 table (lazy 'at once' vs message at tool boundary); Key decisions re-stream — No ordering guarantee across delivery paths. Rejected 3-0: lazy is a separate passive class by design (TRUST-POLICY A8, D5 'starts no turn'); the spec makes no per-thread FIFO promise; each item is framed with id, thread and sender.
- D5 'Attach to the next main-conversation tool.call result as context' — Attach-once undefined under parallel tool calls. Rejected 3-0: D5's delivered-id set and the D10 at-most-once invariant cover duplicates in a single-threaded mod; splitting across results is harmless; the denied-call case is the separate confirmed finding above.
- D1 'spawns herdr-threads watch'; D8 'versioned with the binary' — Binary location and mod/CLI version skew unspecified. Rejected 2-1: same PATH convention as the existing hooks; skew fails safe to native wake via exit codes and the MOD_WATCH gate.
